summary: D-6 cupola lookout in the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness built 1924, where Norman Maclean once staffed, abandoned in 1967 and kept standing by volunteer restoration.

facts.status_note: Abandoned as an active lookout in 1967; cabin preserved through volunteer restoration, not staffed or rentable.

access.note: Remote wilderness hike via Friday Pass; not drive-up, not rentable.

visit.trail_note: Reached by a demanding hike from Friday Pass into the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness.

events.note: Peak first used for fire detection.
Norman Maclean staffed the lookout, later the basis for his novella about the job.
D-6 cupola groundhouse constructed (one source says 1923).
Lookout abandoned as an active fire detection post.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, November 24, 1995.
Volunteers, Forest Service staff, and Iowa high school students replaced the roof, main-level flooring, and door, hauling materials in by mule train and on foot.
Lookout wrapped for fire protection during the 2021 fire season; a foundation corner stabilized.

evidence.supports: Peak first used 1914; D-6 cupola built 1924; 8,062 ft elevation
evidence.quote: The 8,062' peak was first used in 1914 for fire detection and the 12'x12' groundhouse was constructed in 1924.
The site was featured in a story recounted in the book: "A River Runs Through It" by Norman McLean, who worked as a lookout on Grave Peak in 1919.

evidence.supports: Built 1923 per this source; last used 1960s
evidence.quote: this D-6 cupola cabin, built in 1923, was last used in the 1960's
The current cupola cabin on Grave Peak was built in 1924. This is one of the few remaining D6 model lookouts. The lookout was abandoned in 1967.
Norman Maclean famously staffed Grave peak in 1919. It was the inspiration for his semi-autobiographical novella, USFS 1919: The Ranger, the Cook, and a Hole in the Sky.

evidence.supports: 2019 restoration by volunteers, mule train, Iowa students
evidence.quote: In 2019 a group of volunteers, Forest Service employees, interns, and leaders from the Selway-Bitterroot Frank Church Foundation as well as volunteers and high school students from Iowa completed the amazing task of removing and replacing the roof, main level flooring, and a new door.

evidence.supports: Wrapped for fire protection 2021; foundation stabilized
evidence.quote: This unique lookout has been wrapped for fire protection many times over – including this 2021 fire season.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 1924; firelookout.com gives 1923. Both years are stated in the story as a minor discrepancy.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict (1923 vs 1924) noted in the story. No documented staffing list beyond Maclean. Access level set to public/hike-in since it sits in designated wilderness with no restriction mentioned, but it's a serious approach, not a casual visit.
